raw_response:
I’m already old, and with only 4.1 mu and two people in the house, I can’t spread myself too thin. This year I’ll still keep cotton as the main crop, because I know that crop best and if I manage it steadily it still brings cash. But I won’t push fertilizer too hard. Cotton can respond to more input, but fertilizer, water, and spray all cost money, and at my age I’d rather keep a safer, manageable plan. Millet I keep on a small piece because it is steady, doesn’t ask for much water, and if the weather turns bad it usually still gives me something. Mungbean I also keep because it is light on fertilizer, easy to manage, and the money comes back quickly if the stand is good. I have a well, so I can irrigate, but pumping costs money, so I will use water mainly at the key times, not casually. What I do is mostly what has worked on my land before: cotton gets basal fertilizer and then one topdress, millet gets a lighter dose, and mungbean I keep simple, mostly watching weeds and insects. I’d rather earn a bit less than spend too much and worry all season.
